Vase by Jean Dunand

Jean Dunand’s dark metal vase covered in a dense all-over pattern of inlaid silver zigzags, meanders, and sunbursts.

Context

The Art Institute records the vase as c. 1925, copper and silver inlay, 28.6 × 12.7 cm, by Jean Dunand (French, 1877–1942), Paris. Style: Art Deco. Credit: Gift of Arthur T. Aldis and Russell Tyson. Art Institute of Chicago.

The AIC API marks the object as not in the public domain. AIC API.

Observed

  • The vase is a tall ovoid with a narrow flared neck; the metal is dark gray-brown with a soft sheen.
  • Thin lighter lines of inlay cover the whole surface in a dense pattern of zigzags, stepped meanders, concentric arcs, and small star or sun shapes.
  • The pattern is irregular and all-over, not arranged in bands or panels.
  • There is no color other than the dark ground and the lighter inlay.

Why it belongs

The inlay is a catalogue of Deco motifs in one object: zigzag, step, arc, and sunburst, drawn as light line on a dark metal ground.

Its free, all-over layout is looser than the symmetrical Deco rubric; it shows the influence of African and Cubist pattern on French decorative art.

Borrow

Fill a dark surface with thin light-line zigzags and steps as a texture.

Limit the palette to one dark metal ground and one lighter line color.
